worksheet.title: Move Blocks
worksheet.subtitle: Each block points the way Bit goes
worksheet.learning_goal: I can match a move block to the way it makes Bit go.

parts.title: One block, one way
parts.text: A move block tells Bit ONE way to go. ➡ moves Bit RIGHT. ⬅ moves Bit LEFT. ⬆ moves Bit UP. ⬇ moves Bit DOWN. One block makes one step in one direction.

parts.title: The move blocks
parts.note: Four move blocks. Each arrow points the way Bit will travel.

parts.title: Find UP
parts.prompt: Circle the move block that makes Bit go UP.

parts.title: Find LEFT
parts.prompt: Circle the move block that makes Bit go to the LEFT.

parts.title: An empty block
parts.note: This block has no arrow yet.

parts.title: You try
parts.prompt: Bit wants to go DOWN. Draw the arrow in the empty block that tells Bit to go DOWN. It points ⬇.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Each move block points the way Bit goes. To make Bit move a certain way, you pick the block with that arrow. That is how you tell a computer exactly what to do.

teacher_guide.eyebrow: Teacher Guide · Kindergarten · Intro Block Coding
teacher_guide.title: Move Blocks
teacher_guide.subtitle: Quick facilitation notes & answer key

parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children learn the move blocks: each arrow block makes Bit travel in exactly one direction — right, left, up, or down. Matching a symbol to one exact action is the start of reading code. No coding experience needed.

parts.title: Before you start (no computer needed)
parts.text: No computer — paper, a pencil, and a crayon. You read each prompt aloud. Optional: paper blocks (a green flag block + arrow blocks) to stack by hand, or floor boxes the child can walk.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 1. Show them (you do). Hold up each arrow block and act it out: up arrow → step up, left arrow → step left.
2. Do one together. Exercise 1 — the up block makes Bit go up.
3. Let them try. Children find the left block (Ex 2), then draw a down arrow (Ex 3).

parts.title: Answer key (these are the verified correct answers)
text: Exercise 1 — the up block (arrow points up). Exercise 2 — the left block (arrow points left).
Exercise 3 — the down block: the child draws an arrow pointing straight down in the empty block.

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: mixing up left and right. Step it out with the child to check.
Make it easier: use four arrow cards and walk each direction on the floor.
Make it harder: call a direction and have the child draw the matching arrow.
Make it active: play "arrow says" — children step the direction of each arrow you hold up.

parts.title: Ontario Kindergarten link (official wording)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children use directional language and symbols to describe movement.
In plain terms: each arrow block moves Bit one way (right, left, up, or down).
No reading is needed from the child — you read each prompt aloud; the child circles, numbers, or draws an arrow.

parts.title: You'll know it worked when
parts.text: The child matches each arrow block to its direction and draws the down arrow correctly.
